A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same signal-propagation theory for Transformers. All 27 pages of each version, including equations, figures, algorithms, and Appendices A–C, support comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original TinyStories training experiments, attention and gradient simulations, and supplementary experiments on gain control, learning rates, and infinite-depth propagation.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds training-loss curves and empirical signal-propagation measurements in autoregressive Transformers.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, query/key initialization scaling, and gain-controlled attention retain their procedures. The expanded Section 4 largely restates block-update equations already present in v2's appendix; the causal experiment applies the existing prediction framework.

E1.justification: Appendix C.6 adds signal-propagation tests under causal attention, including early and late token positions. This is a focused extension beyond v2's encoder experiments. TinyStories masked-language modeling is retained; no additional corpus or autoregressive language-model training task is reported.

E2.justification: The vanilla versus gain-controlled comparison remains unchanged (v2 Figure C.1; v3 Figure 6), as do the pre-/post-LayerNorm comparisons in Figure 4. The new diagnostics and causal experiment introduce no additional competing method.

E3.justification: The new causal protocol uses a 50-layer post-norm model, width 720, approximately 200-token sequences, and β = 0.5, 2, 3, comparing first-50, full-sequence, and last-50 averages. Section 5 changes the gain-control experiment's depth from 20 to 30, matching its existing caption/settings without establishing a rerun. Figure 1e's new β = 0.1 label conflicts with the retained Appendix A.1 value of approximately 0.02.

E4.justification: Figure 12 adds a focused applicability analysis testing where the two-parameter theory succeeds or fails under causal masking. Figures 10–11 add training-loss diagnostics for existing experiments. The spectral, reduced-learning-rate, and infinite-depth analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Repeated-initialization averaging and error bars were already reported in v2. V3's causal experiment uses the existing practice of averaging over 10 initializations and 10 sequences. Existing run counts remain unchanged, and no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Figures 10–11 newly report training-loss trajectories for the experiments in Figures 1e and 3b. Figure 12 adds position-dependent findings, reporting tighter concentration and better theoretical agreement for late tokens. Existing plotted results are retained; these additions do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Result 1 explicitly adds the infinite-width limit alongside infinite sequence length. V3 corrects the attention-score covariance normalization in Section 3.1 and the query/key variance expression in Appendix B.1, from σa²/d to σa/d. The principal results and derivations otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the unified explanation of rank and entropy collapse, REM mapping, gradient analysis, trainability algorithms, and three principal case studies. The conclusion is shortened, but its omitted trainability statement remains elsewhere in the paper.

C2.justification: V3 adds a substantive causal-model boundary: early-token geometry is inadequately described by two parameters, while late tokens admit the approximation. It also reframes the gradient explanation around disruption of simplex geometry, explicitly limits the vanishing-gradient result to initialization, and adds guidance on combining gain control with edge-of-chaos MLP initialization.

D1.justification: Appendix C.6 documents the new causal experiment's hidden and MLP sizes, ReLU activation, weight/bias variances, residual strengths, and sequence sampling. Existing hardware, optimizer, and masked-language-modeling details are retained. No change in code or data access information is evident.

R1.justification: V3 adds Vershynin's High-dimensional Probability as support for concentration arguments in Section 2. Other cited works and the positioning against earlier Transformer theories are retained; the related-work relocation and citation-style conversion do not constitute substantive positioning changes.

P1.justification: V3 separates related work and contributions, moves sequence-geometry definitions into Section 2, and brings MLP recursions from the appendix into Section 4. It rewrites selected explanations and corrects wording, while retaining most narrative and proof text.

P2.justification: The document receives an extensive ICLR-format layout revision, including title styling, running headers, typography, text sizing, and figure placement. Figure 1 is recomposed with an added parameter legend, and Figures 10–12 are added. Existing appendix plots are retained and renumbered rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: V3 clarifies asymptotic assumptions, corrects scaling expressions, and adds evidence identifying the causal extension's applicability limits in Figure 12. The added training curves and more self-contained block analysis improve transparency. These are bounded gains: the central evidence is retained, and inconsistencies such as Figure 1e's β label versus Appendix A.1 still limit reporting clarity.
